svg.title: Western Gulf · Layered exchange
svg.desc: Freshwater surplus drives surface export through deep straits, above a cold, saltier inflow. Qualitative adopted model; no measured speed, depth, or transport.

g.text: Freshwater surplus drives surface export through deep straits, above a cold, saltier inflow.
Both layers use the deep passage.
Mixing exchanges heat and salt between them.
Net export includes the river and rain surplus.
Wind and tides can reverse local flow temporarily.
No depth, layer thickness or current speed is assigned.
Along west-facing Cymean shores, southward winds favor offshore transport and localized upwelling.
The opposing east-facing shores favor onshore transport and downwelling. Headlands and seabed modify the pattern.
Cooling erodes thermal layering; freshwater can still preserve a surface-to-depth density contrast.
Runoff and increasing light support coastal growth; river timing varies between catchments.
Warm surface layers coexist with cool upwelling patches; the net two-layer strait exchange persists.
Cooling and wet spells reshape layering and plumes without assigning a permanent gulf-wide loop.
NAVIGATION · Outbound ships gain current help; inbound ships need useful wind. Opposing waves steepen in the straits.
The plan-view arrows share one corridor; the section shows their vertical separation. Small map hexes: 24 miles face to face.
